title: Five-hour Office: The One-Person Conglomerate
summary: An offline five-venture decision lab with a hard 300-minute week, editable assumptions, explicit infeasibility and sensitivity, planned demand tests, and an original working Ledgerleaf CSV checker.
limitations: All seed venture facts, audiences, ordinal scores and confidence values are synthetic; no customers, revenue, outreach or market validation are claimed.
The user's 300-minute week is a separate extension of a 40-hour seed. New narrow-scope estimates are unmeasured; the original reserve and ten experiment rows remain frozen.

The recommendation is a heuristic for one artifact, not an optimizer of revenue, an approval, or a native Hive task completion. Reuse scores may double-count benefits and timing ignores unknown rework.
Demand tests are plans only. Future execution estimates exclude recruitment and are not funded in this week's plan; approval and consent would be needed.
Only Ledgerleaf's offering is implemented. Selecting another simulated winner does not create another product or validate any demand claim.
CSV checks are structural, case-sensitive and conservative; they do not repair or sanitize input, execute formulas, certify accounting or guarantee import compatibility.
The browser UI needs the repo-root HTTP preview for local ES modules and JSON. No external resources or runtime dependencies are used; no preview service was started here.
Automated UI coverage uses a local DOM harness, not a real browser or accessibility certification. Visual browser review remains unperformed.
